title: The Travels of Benjamin of Tudela
intro: Benjamin of Tudela, a Jewish traveller from the Kingdom of Navarre, set out from the northeast of the Iberian Peninsula around 1165, perhaps on a pilgrimage to the Holy Land. He recorded the Jewish communities of the towns he passed through, with their numbers and leaders.
ending: He returned to the Iberian Peninsula in 1173 and described his years abroad in The Travels of Benjamin. Scholars do not agree on his exact route.

stops.text: The journey began at Zaragoza, in the valley of the Ebro. Benjamin set out from the northeast of the Iberian Peninsula around 1165, in what may have begun as a pilgrimage to the Holy Land.
stops.quote: His journey began in Zaragoza, farther down the valley of the Ebro to Tarragona

stops.text: He went farther down the valley of the Ebro to Tarragona, the next town on his route.
stops.quote: His journey began in Zaragoza, farther down the valley of the Ebro to Tarragona, Barcelona, and Girona

stops.text: Barcelona followed Tarragona on his way. At each town he stopped to meet people, describe occupations and count the Jews who lived there.
stops.quote: He stopped frequently, meeting people, visiting places, describing occupations, and giving a demographic count of Jews in each town and country that he visited.

stops.text: From Girona he turned north into France, on the way to the port from which he sailed.
stops.quote: Tarragona, Barcelona, and Girona, whence he proceeded north to France

stops.text: After crossing France he set sail from Marseille, leaving the western Mediterranean coast for Italy.
stops.quote: whence he proceeded north to France, then set sail from Marseille.

stops.text: Genoa was the first of the Italian cities he visited after sailing from Marseille.
stops.quote: After visiting Genoa, Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Rome

stops.text: He visited Lucca on the way south through Italy, after sailing from Marseille and visiting Genoa.
stops.quote: After visiting Genoa, Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Rome

stops.text: He visited Pisa after Lucca, still on his way south through Italy to Rome.
stops.quote: After visiting Genoa, Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Rome

stops.text: Florence was his next stop in Italy after Pisa, and the last before Rome.
stops.quote: After visiting Genoa, Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Rome

stops.text: Rome was the last place he visited in Italy before going on to Greece and Constantinople.
stops.quote: After visiting Genoa, Lucca, Pisa, Florence and Rome, he went to Greece and Constantinople, then set off across Asia.

stops.text: After Greece he reached Constantinople, and from there set off across Asia.
stops.quote: he went to Greece and Constantinople, then set off across Asia.

stops.text: He crossed Syria, Lebanon, the Land of Israel and northern Mesopotamia, which he called Shinar. His visit to the ruins outside Mosul is one of the earliest accurate descriptions of the site of ancient Nineveh.
stops.quote: His visit to the ruins outside Mosul is one of the earliest accurate descriptions of the site of ancient Nineveh.

stops.text: He reached Baghdad, which he described with great enthusiasm, noting in particular the virtues of the Caliph.
stops.quote: In his accounts, Benjamin of Tudela describes Baghdad with great enthusiasm, making particular note of the virtues of the Caliph.

stops.text: From Baghdad he went to Persia. Susa is among the places of importance in Jewish history that he visited.
stops.quote: He visited 300 cities in all, including many of importance in Jewish history, such as Susa, Sura, and Pumbedita.

notes: The article gives the route as one list of places with no dates beyond 'around 1165' and the return in 1173; all years are therefore estimates and the stops before Susa carry c. 1165 as a placeholder of the route's stage, not a date the article gives (Mosul, Baghdad and Susa carry date between 1165 and 1173, year 1173, which are the article's bounds, not a known date). Most stops rest on a list, with little that happened at each place. Left out: Greece, Syria, Lebanon, Land of Israel, Persia (regions); the return across Arabia to Egypt and North Africa and back to Iberia in 1173 (regions); Sura and Pumbedita (named, order of visit not given); Laish/Baniyas (his identification is disputed). The article says scholars disagree on his exact route and on where in Africa he went. Zaragoza: the article says the journey began there; it also says he set out from the northeast Iberian Peninsula. Genoa, Lucca, Marseille have no entry in places.tsv.
